abstract: Summary Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is an autoimmune disorder, and despite the availability of multiple Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved therapies, current clinical needs remain unmet. In this study, we find that caseinolytic protease P (ClpP) expression is markedly upregulated in colonic tissues from IBD patients and preclinical colitis models, particularly in CD4 + T cells. Subsequently, a small molecule, namely NCA029, is identified, and its therapeutic efficacy and mechanism of action are investigated both in vitro and in vivo . Oral administration of NCA029 significantly alleviates symptoms associated with dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced acute and interleukin (IL)-10-deficient chronic colitis. The effects of NCA029 are largely dependent on its selective binding to ClpP in CD4 + T cells, thereby mitigating inflammation and restoring intestinal barrier function. Furthermore, NCA029 activates ClpP to promote oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) inhibition and concomitantly modulate the Th17/Treg balance. In conclusion, our study develops a therapeutic strategy for treating IBD through the chemical activation of ClpP.

Six-week-old germ-free male C57BL/6JGpt/-Il10em1Cd4885/Gp mice (model #T005959; GemPharmatech) were acquired and housed in a specific pathogen–free room on a ventilated microisolator rack. Microbe strains
The Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) strain was used in this study. The strain was preserved by our lab. The strain is cultured in lysogeny broth (LB) medium (10 g/L sodium chloride, 10 g/L tryptone, and 5 g/L yeast extract).
UC patients
Tissue samples were provided by the tissue bank of the West China Hospital in accordance with the regulations of the tissue biobank and the approval of the ethics committee of the Sichuan University. The study was written informed consent was obtained from all patients. For this study, six male human participants were included, divided into two groups: a control group and a UC (ulcerative colitis) group. Sample allocation was based on clinical pathological examination results; participants with inflammatory lesions were assigned to the UC group. Control Group: Three male patients, aged 46, 60, and 69 years, all of Han Chinese ethnicity. UC Group: Three male patients, aged 57, 57, and 56 years, all of Han Chinese ethnicity.
Method details
DSS colitis model
6-8-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were used. Colitis was induced by administration of 2.5% DSS (Mw:36000–50000 Da; MP Biomedicals, 02160110-CF) in the drinking water for a period of 5–7 days, followed by exposure to freshwater. NCA029 was administered by oral gavage once daily at doses of 5, 10 and 20 mL/kg; Tofacitinib (20 mg/kg) was administered by gavage twice daily; the vehicle (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil and 90% saline) was given by gavage once daily. The mice were subjected to daily monitoring of their body weight, stool consistency, and rectal bleeding, with each parameter being assigned a score ranging from 0 to 4. These individual scores were then combined to generate a composite DAI score. The specific metrics used for scoring were as follows:
The body weight score is categorized as follows: 0 indicates a weight loss of less than 1% from the initial study day; 1 represents a weight loss ranging from 1% to 5%; 2 denotes a weight loss between 5% and 10%; 3 signifies a weight loss ranging from 10% to 15%; and 4 indicates a weight loss exceeding 15%.
The stool consistency score is categorized as follows: 0 represents firm stool; 1 indicates slightly soft stool; 2 denotes very soft but formed stool; 3 signifies very soft and unformed stool; and 4 represents watery diarrhea.
Bleeding score: 0 = none; 1 = mild occult blood in stools; 2 = moderate occult blood in stools; 3 = significant blood in stools; 4 = predominantly bloody stools.
In addition, mice were given 200 μL of 2.5% DSS by gavage twice daily, thus minimizing within-group variation due to differences in water intake. After 7 days, NCA029 was administered by gavage once daily for treatment. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.
IL-10 KO colitis model
Six-week-old germ-free male C57BL/6JGpt/-Il10em1Cd4885/Gp mice were used. After the twelfth week, mice were randomly divided into two experimental groups and monitored daily for the presence of spontaneous colitis. Specific parameters measured included body weight, fecal consistency, and presence/absence of fecal occult blood. Mice were treated with either a carrier (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil 90% physiological saline) or 20 mg/kg of NCA029 once daily by oral gavage. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.

Histology
Haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining by were used to examine pathological changes in the colon. In the 2.5% DSS and IL-10 KO study, colonic cross-sections were scored using a reported scoring scale that grades inflammation (0–5), glandular detachment (0–5), and erosions/ulcers (0–5).
Masson staining was used to detect collagen fibers and inflammatory cell infiltration in colonic tissue. In Masson staining, sections were stained by Masson Stain Kit (G1340, Solarbio, China). All operations were performed according to the instructions.
Immunohistochemistry (IHC) involves several essential steps, including specimen preparation, antigen retrieval, blocking, primary antibody incubation, washing, and secondary antibody incubation. Detection of the immune response is achieved by utilizing an HRP-conjugated secondary antibody and employing a DAB substrate kit for chromogenic visualization. Alternatively, fluorescence detection is performed using an appropriate fluorescently labeled secondary antibody.
The TUNEL staining kit is employed for the detection of apoptotic cell populations. This method involves the labeling of DNA fragmentation ends, enabling the identification and quantitative analysis of apoptotic cells. The procedural steps include tissue sectioning, proteinase K treatment, TUNEL reaction, incubation, reaction termination, and fluorescence staining.
The pathological assessment was performed using a whole tissue section scanning system (3DHISTECH, Pannoramic MIDI) at 10× or 20× magnification. Images were randomly captured under the selected fields of view using the CaseViewer software. For the analysis of IHC protein expression, ImageJ was employed to quantify relative expression levels based on grayscale values.
Serum chemokine analysis
On the last day of colitis induction, mice whole blood was collected and centrifuged. The quantitative analysis of IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β in mouse serum was performed using the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit according to the product manuals.
ClpP enzymatic assays
Human ClpP (HsClpP) was cloned and transformed into Escherichia coli with an N-terminal SUMO tag (excluding the MTS sequence). Initially, the cultures were expanded in LB medium containing 40 μg/mL kanamycin at 37°C and 220 rpm. Subsequently, the cells were exposed to overnight treatment with 0.1 mM isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) at 16°C. The E. coli cells were collected, sonicated in a buffer (25 mM Tris-2HCl, pH 8.0, 0.5 M NaCl), and the precipitate was eliminated through centrifugation. After the Ulp1 tag was removed, the proteins were subsequently bound to the supernatant using Ni-NTA column chromatography. Followed, additional purification steps were conducted, including ion exchange and molecular sieve, to eliminate the tag.
In the peptidase activity assay, the detection system consists of 0.5 μM ClpP, 100 μM substrate (AC-WLA-AMC), buffer (25 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 0.5 M NaCl), and a compound. Fluorescence readings are taken at 380/460 nm every 5 min for 30 min. The relative activity of the peptidase is normalized by the fluorescence intensity corresponding to the condition without the compound. 2

To assess the hydrolytic activity of NCA029 on α-casein, a reaction mixture containing NCA029, 5 μM HsClpP, and 40 μM α-casein was incubated at 30°C for 1 h. Subsequently, SDS-PAGE and R250 staining were performed. The concentrations of NCA029 were 1.56, 3.13, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100 and 200 μM, and the EC
50

Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) assay
In the ITC experiments, a Nano-ITC system (manufactured by Nano, USA) was utilized. The experimental procedure entailed the gradual addition of the test compound into the sample cell at a concentration of 10 μM, with a volume of 200 μL. Following this, an injection syringe was employed to introduce 50 μL of HsClpP at a concentration of 100 μM into the sample cell, facilitating the titration process. The acquired data were subsequently subjected to fitting analysis utilizing LaunchNano Analyze software, leading to the determination of relevant parameters.

To investigate the binding affinity of NCA029 to HsClpP (PDB:
6DL7
), we conducted molecular dynamics simulations (MD). The simulations were initiated with a 1000 ps equilibration period at a temperature of 300 K to achieve system stability. Subsequently, a constant restraining force of 1000 kJ mol

This was followed by a 500 ps NVT equilibrium and a 500 ps NPT equilibrium to confine the overall system positions. Finally, extensive MD simulations of 100 ns duration were performed at a temperature of 300 K.
Prior to simulation, energy minimization was executed using the Steepest Descent Method under vacuum conditions. The system was then immersed in a cubic water box, ensuring a 1.0 nm distance between the complex and the box’s edges. Charge neutralization of the system was achieved through the introduction of chloride or sodium ions. Protein structure and binding cavity analyses were conducted using PyMOL software.
Quantitative RT-PCR
Total RNA was extracted from collected cells using Trizol reagent. Cells were treated with RNAiso, followed by chloroform addition and centrifugation. Isopropanol was then added to the supernatant for RNA precipitation, which was dissolved in DEPC water for storage. A 2-min reaction at 42°C eliminated genomic DNA, and reverse transcription was performed using SYBR Green on a PCR machine at 37°C for 15 min, with a 5-s denaturation at 85°C and final equilibrium at 4°C. The subsequent PCR reaction was conducted according to the provided protocol, using the following primer sequences: STAT3- Forward Primer: 5′-CAGCAGCTTGACACACGGTA-3’; STAT3- Reverse Primer:5′- AAACACCAAAGTGGCATGTGA-3’.
Immunoblotting
After collecting and washing cells or tissues, they were lysed with lysis buffer and centrifuged at 12,000 rpm at 4°C, discarding the precipitate. Protein concentration was determined using a BCA assay kit and adjusted to the same level. An appropriate loading buffer was added, and proteins were denatured at 100°C. A total of 40 μg of protein was used for SDS-PAGE separation, followed by transfer onto a PVDF membrane at 100 V and blocking with skimmed milk. After overnight incubation with the primary antibody, the membrane was incubated with the secondary antibody for 2 h at room temperature and imaged for immunoblotting. Band gray value analysis was conducted using ImageJ software to calculate relative expression, with β-actin and GAPDH as internal controls.

Cell viability assay
After drug treatment, cells were subjected to the replacement of the original culture medium with 10% Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) working solution. The supernatant in the blank wells was also replaced with CCK-8 working solution to eliminate background interference. Subsequently, the cells were incubated at 37°C for a duration ranging from 30 to 150 min. Finally, absorbance was measured at a wavelength of 450 nm, and cell viability was calculated.
Apoptosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement
After cellular treatment with drug administration, apoptosis and intracellular ROS were analyzed using flow cytometry. The accumulation of intracellular ROS was measured with an ROS detection kit (Solarbio, Beijing, China), with an excitation wavelength of 488 nm and an emission wavelength of 525 nm. Annexin V-FITC/Propidium Iodide (Beyotime, Nanjing, China) was employed to detect cell apoptosis. The excitation wavelength for Annexin V-FITC was 488 nm, and the emission wavelength was 525 nm, while for Propidium Iodide, the excitation wavelength was 488 nm, and the emission wavelength was 630 nm.
Oxygen consumption rate (OCR) assay
According to the manufacturer’s instructions, the Agilent Seahorse XF Cell Mito Stress Test Kit (Agilent Technologies) was employed to measure cellular OCR. In brief, post-drug treatment, cells were equilibrated for 60 min at 37°C in a CO
2
-free incubator using XF analysis medium (Agilent Technologies) supplemented with 10 mM glucose, 100 mM pyruvate, and 200 mM L-glutamine. Subsequently, cells were transferred to the XF96 Seahorse XF Bioanalyzer (Agilent Technologies). Following the initiation of measurements, cells were sequentially injected with 1.5 μM oligomycin, 0.75 μM carbonyl cyanide
p
-trifluoromethoxyphenylhydrazone (FCCP), and a mixture of 0.5 μM rotenone and antimycin A. After measurement completion, the supernatant was removed, and the remaining cellular protein concentration was quantified using the BCA protein assay kit. Normalization of OCR results to protein concentration was performed, and further analysis was conducted using Wave software (Agilent Technologies).
Determination of ETC complex activity and ATP content
After drug treatment, the culture medium was carefully aspirated, and cells were washed three times with pre-chilled PBS. Each well received lysing buffer from the assay kit, and cell lysis was ensured through reverse pipetting until no resistance was felt. The supernatant was centrifuged at 4°C and 12,000 rpm for 15 min. In a black 96-well plate, 100 μL of working solution was added to each well and allowed to stand at room temperature for 5 min. A standard curve was created using gradient dilutions of the provided standard solution. Next, 20 μL of samples and diluted standards were added to each well, mixed, and incubated for 5 min. Luminescence values were measured using a multifunctional microplate reader. Finally, protein concentrations were quantified using a NanoDrop, and ATP concentrations were calculated based on the standard curve, adjusted for protein concentrations.
According to the instructions of manufacturer, the CheKine Mitochondrial Complex I, III, and IV Activity Colorimetric Assay Kits were employed for the quantification of the activity levels of NADH-coenzyme Q oxidoreductase (Complex I), Q-cytochrome c oxidoreductase (Complex III), and cytochrome
c
oxidase (Complex IV). The specific operational procedures can be referenced from relevant literature reports.
Cell transfection experiments
During transfection, it is crucial to have suspended cells in the logarithmic growth phase. Utilize Opti-MEM medium to dilute Lipofectamine 3000 reagent, ensuring thorough mixing. Dilute DNA in Opti-MEM medium to prepare a DNA premix, then add P3000 reagent and mix thoroughly. Incorporate the diluted DNA into the pre-diluted Lipofectamine 3000 reagent at a 1:1 ratio, incubating at room temperature for 10–15 min. Gradually add the DNA-lipid complex dropwise to the cells and incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 culture chamber for 48 h. Subsequent experiments involve the utilization of CD4

Intestinal flora analysis
After model completion, the mouse gut microbiota in the DSS free drinking water model was analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The workflow involved sample collection, DNA extraction, PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, data processing, sequence clustering, taxonomic annotation, bioinformatics analysis, and results presentation. Fecal samples from the control, DSS model, and NCA029 high-dose groups were collected and stored at −80°C. DNA was extracted using a reagent kit, and primers for the 16S rDNA V4 region (515F and 806R) were used for amplification. The NEBNext Ultra II DNA Library Prep Kit was employed for library preparation. High-throughput sequencing generated extensive 16S rRNA gene sequences, followed by data processing to remove low-quality sequences and generate an OTU table for taxonomic annotation. Bioinformatics analysis assessed microbial community composition, abundance, and diversity through methods like Alpha and Beta diversity, PCoA, and LEfSe analysis. Results were visualized in charts or heatmaps to show gut microbiota composition and changes.
Proteomic analysis
The proteomic analysis was entrusted to Shanghai BIOPROFILE. After the cell collection, samples were lysed using SDT lysis buffer, followed by boiling, ultrasonication, and additional boiling. After centrifugation, the supernatant was collected and quantified using a BCA Protein Assay Kit. Protein digestion involved FASP method, and resulting peptides were desalted for LC-MS analysis. LC-MS/MS was performed using a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer, and data were analyzed with MaxQuant against the UniProtKB Rattus norvegicus database. Proteins with ≥1.5-fold change and
p

DSS colitis model
6-8-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were used. Colitis was induced by administration of 2.5% DSS (Mw:36000–50000 Da; MP Biomedicals, 02160110-CF) in the drinking water for a period of 5–7 days, followed by exposure to freshwater. NCA029 was administered by oral gavage once daily at doses of 5, 10 and 20 mL/kg; Tofacitinib (20 mg/kg) was administered by gavage twice daily; the vehicle (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil and 90% saline) was given by gavage once daily. The mice were subjected to daily monitoring of their body weight, stool consistency, and rectal bleeding, with each parameter being assigned a score ranging from 0 to 4. These individual scores were then combined to generate a composite DAI score. The specific metrics used for scoring were as follows:
The body weight score is categorized as follows: 0 indicates a weight loss of less than 1% from the initial study day; 1 represents a weight loss ranging from 1% to 5%; 2 denotes a weight loss between 5% and 10%; 3 signifies a weight loss ranging from 10% to 15%; and 4 indicates a weight loss exceeding 15%.
The stool consistency score is categorized as follows: 0 represents firm stool; 1 indicates slightly soft stool; 2 denotes very soft but formed stool; 3 signifies very soft and unformed stool; and 4 represents watery diarrhea.
Bleeding score: 0 = none; 1 = mild occult blood in stools; 2 = moderate occult blood in stools; 3 = significant blood in stools; 4 = predominantly bloody stools.
In addition, mice were given 200 μL of 2.5% DSS by gavage twice daily, thus minimizing within-group variation due to differences in water intake. After 7 days, NCA029 was administered by gavage once daily for treatment. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.
IL-10 KO colitis model
Six-week-old germ-free male C57BL/6JGpt/-Il10em1Cd4885/Gp mice were used. After the twelfth week, mice were randomly divided into two experimental groups and monitored daily for the presence of spontaneous colitis. Specific parameters measured included body weight, fecal consistency, and presence/absence of fecal occult blood. Mice were treated with either a carrier (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil 90% physiological saline) or 20 mg/kg of NCA029 once daily by oral gavage. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.

Introduction
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, relapsing, and life-limiting condition of disorders that affects a significant number of people worldwide, with an increasing global occurrence.
1
IBD encompasses two primary subtypes: Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), both of which are distinguished by persistent inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract.
2
Although the exact cause of IBD remains uncertain, it is widely recognized that an improper immune response plays a crucial role in the development of these disorders.
3
,
4
CD4
+
T cells, which are essential regulators of the adaptive immune system, are known to significantly contribute to this process.
5
In particular, the balance between two CD4
+
T cell subsets, Th17 cells and regulatory T cells (Treg cells), plays a crucial role in determining the course of IBD.
6
,
7
Th17 cells, a specific subset of effector CD4
+
T cells, play a vital role in defending against extracellular pathogens.
8
Nonetheless, dysfunctional Th17 cell activity is implicated in the development of chronic inflammatory disorders such as multiple sclerosis, IBD, and rheumatoid arthritis.
9
,
10
,
11
Conversely, Treg cells expressing Foxp3 exert inhibitory effects on inflammatory responses and contribute to protection against autoimmune diseases.
12
An imbalance characterized by an excessive presence of Th17 cells compared to Treg cells has been observed in affected individuals, which correlates with the persistence of intestinal inflammation.
13
Consequently, the positive regulation of Th17 and Treg cell balance significantly impacts the progression of IBD. Currently, the main targeted therapy methods include inhibiting the differentiation and proliferation of Th17 cells, neutralizing or inhibiting cytokines produced by Th17 cells, inhibiting the migration of Th17 cells, and using probiotics to stabilize intestinal flora. Most of the findings were consistent with experimental expectations, but inhibition of IL-17A sometimes produced conflicting results.
6
Therefore, it is necessary to further regulate the differentiation and function of Th17 cells with the aim of providing therapeutic targets for IBD treatment.
Metabolism plays a crucial role in the functioning of immune cells, with glycolysis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) serving as the principal bioenergetic pathways within the cell. Distinct metabolic profiles are linked to specific immune cell outcomes and functions.
14
Although earlier research predominantly indicated that Th17 cells depend on glycolysis, mounting evidence suggests that Th17 cells necessitate OXPHOS for lineage differentiation and pathogenicity.
15
,
16
Recent research suggests that mitochondrial respiration is essential for the regulation of glycolysis, TCA (tricarboxylic acid) cycling, and Th17-mediated inflammation during Th17 cell differentiation.
14
,
17
Inhibition of mitochondrial OXPHOS has been found to hinder Th17 cell differentiation and result in a functionally suppressive Treg cell, thereby presenting a potential therapeutic approach for treating IBD.
17
,
18
The ATP-dependent mitochondrial caseinolytic protease P (ClpP) is situated within the mitochondrial matrix and regulates the quantity of mitochondrial proteins.
19
In mammals, several respiratory chain subunit proteins, including ubiquitous cytochrome
c
reductase core protein I (UQCRC1), succinate dehydrogenase complex iron sulfur subunit B (SDHB), NADH dehydrogenase 1 beta subcomplex subunit 8 (NDUFB8), and ATP synthase subunit alpha (ATP5A), have been identified as substrates of ClpP.
20
,
21
,
22
,
23
The hydrolysis of substrates is seemingly enhanced by chemical agonism of ClpP, leading to an impact on the functioning of the mitochondrial respiratory chain and regulating OXPHOS.
24
Indeed, our previous investigations have demonstrated that chemical agonism of human ClpP (HsClpP) disrupts mitochondrial OXPHOS by hydrolyzing subunits of the mitochondrial respiratory chain, such as SDHB, which was employed to be an ideal antitumor therapeutic.
20
However, the specific effects of the agonist on immune cells, especially CD4
+
T cell subsets, remain to be elucidated. Thus, targeting ClpP has potential to inhibit differentiation of Th17 cells through regulating OXPHOS of CD4
+
T cells.
In this study, we have identified abnormal ClpP expression in intestinal tissue of IBD patients and animal models with colitis. However, knockdown of ClpP aggravates inflammatory status of colitis of mouse model, which indicates that increased expression of ClpP would be an adaptive response to the development of inflammatory diseases and suggests that activation or supplementation of ClpP would improve colitis. Thus, chemical activation by a drug-like ClpP agonist NCA029 was employed to inhibit OXPHOS of CD4
+
T cells and differentiation of Th17 cells
in vitro
, which was confirmed by proteomic profiling. Notably, NCA029 exerted exceptional efficacy by alleviating colitis symptoms, including intestinal inflammation and impaired intestinal barrier function, in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model and interleukin (IL)-10 knockout mouse model. Finally, additional adoptive cell transfer investigation further demonstrated that NCA029 works through targeting ClpP of CD4
+
T cells in DSS-induced colitis mouse model. In summary, these findings demonstrated activation of ClpP as a potential therapeutic strategy of IBD and offer a valuable drug candidate, NCA029, for the drug development of IBD.

Moreover, ClpP levels differ between remission and relapse in IBD patients, and, following infliximab treatment, ClpP levels correlate with remission outcomes. These findings indicate that ClpP may have a significant role in the IBD development and remission.

Recent research has revealed that, during the developmental process, Th17 cells exhibit a rapid increase in mitochondrial respiration. Under conditions of OXPHOS inhibition, activated T cells preferentially express Foxp3 rather than Th17 genes, transforming into suppressive Treg cells.

Discussion
In this study, we observed abnormal upregulation of ClpP in both mouse and human IBD, revealing its association with CD4
+
T cells. Simultaneously, we introduced a ClpP agonist, NCA029, which markedly alleviated symptoms associated with DSS-induced and IL-10 knockout colitis models. The therapeutic potential of NCA029 primarily manifested in its ability to modulate immune responses by inhibiting OXPHOS, thereby attenuating inflammation and maintaining intestinal barrier integrity. Our data suggest that activating ClpP may be an effective approach to intervene in IBD.
Under physiological conditions, ClpP forms a specific interaction with its partner ClpX, inducing the ClpXP proteolytic complex responsible for mediating protein turnover.
35
ClpP has been implicated in various diseases, including obesity, cancer, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
27
,
36
ClpP is highly expressed in some tumor cells, and its activation can degrade mitochondrial respiratory chain-associated proteins, disrupting mitochondrial integrity and function, inducing tumor cell death.
37
,
38
CD4
+
T cells, the major source of inflammation in IBD, share high energy metabolism demands with tumor cells.
39
Moreover, single-cell data analysis revealed that inflammation induced high ClpP expression in CD4
+
T cells, allowing ClpP agonists to impact CD4
+
T cells similar to tumor cells, ultimately alleviating inflammation. Currently, the HsClpP agonist ONC201, used for treating tumors, has entered phase 3 clinical trials, with multiple candidate compounds in preclinical studies.
19
We identified a ClpP agonist, NCA029, with higher affinity and activation capabilities than ONC201, potentially serving as a molecular candidate for treating IBD.
Subsequently, we confirmed the favorable therapeutic effects of NCA029 on both acute and chronic colitis, reflected in the reduction of inflammatory responses and the restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, improving colonic structure. Notably, ClpP has been reported to play a crucial role in inflammatory diseases, as the loss of mouse ClpP leads to upregulation of inflammatory factors.
40
We found that NCA029 increases ROS levels and induces apoptosis in DSS-stimulated CD4
+
T cells. Recent study reported the beneficial role of apoptosis in autoimmune diseases for CD4
+
T cells.
28
Furthermore, transient depletion followed by injection of CD4
+
T cells resulted in an exacerbation of inflammation, further confirming the promoting role of CD4
+
T cells in IBD. NCA029 supplement significantly alleviated IBD-related symptoms, while ClpP knockdown abolished the therapeutic effect of NCA029, suggesting that NCA029 targeting ClpP in CD4
+
T cells induces a therapeutic effect on IBD.
Proteomic analysis revealed an increase in the expression of OXPHOS-related proteins in DSS-stimulated CD4
+
T cells, meeting their high energy demands. DSS treatment upregulated the expression of ClpP, which is possibly associated with the increased protein turnover demand within cells. ClpP plays a crucial role in maintaining the integrity of the respiratory chain complexes and OXPHOS function.
38
Indeed, NCA029 treatment reduced the expression of ETC complex subunit proteins induced by DSS, affecting complex activity, inhibiting OXPHOS, and reducing ATP generation. Interestingly, OXPHOS is related to the balance of Th17/Treg, and its inhibition induces a decrease in Th17 and an increase in Treg cells.
17
We detected that the increased demand for OXPHOS occurred during Th17 differentiation. NCA029 inhibited OXPHOS, affecting STAT3/RORγt signaling, reducing the proportion of Th17 cells, promoting Treg cell differentiation, and ultimately exerting anti-inflammatory effects. Modulating the balance of Th17/Treg cells holds promise as a therapeutic target for treating IBD. Indeed, there are several means of intervening in the Th17/Treg balance for the treatment of IBD.
41
,
42
Particularly, our study proposes an approach to modulating Th17/Treg balance by targeting mitochondrial OXPHOS.
Limitations of the study
While our findings show a significant effect of NCA029 treatment on a preclinical colitis model, further validation through additional studies is required before the drug can be considered for clinical use. Additionally, the exclusive use of male animals may limit the generalizability of our findings, as sex differences can influence immune responses and treatment outcomes. Besides, we recognize the limitation of not exploring the underlying epigenetic mechanisms in this study. The complex interplay between immunometabolism and T cell differentiation remains to be fully elucidated. Future research should delve into the underlying epigenetic mechanisms of effects and assess long-term safety and efficacy, building on the promising safety and efficacy demonstrated in early studies, before translating these findings into clinical applications.

Method details
DSS colitis model
6-8-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were used. Colitis was induced by administration of 2.5% DSS (Mw:36000–50000 Da; MP Biomedicals, 02160110-CF) in the drinking water for a period of 5–7 days, followed by exposure to freshwater. NCA029 was administered by oral gavage once daily at doses of 5, 10 and 20 mL/kg; Tofacitinib (20 mg/kg) was administered by gavage twice daily; the vehicle (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil and 90% saline) was given by gavage once daily. The mice were subjected to daily monitoring of their body weight, stool consistency, and rectal bleeding, with each parameter being assigned a score ranging from 0 to 4. These individual scores were then combined to generate a composite DAI score. The specific metrics used for scoring were as follows:
The body weight score is categorized as follows: 0 indicates a weight loss of less than 1% from the initial study day; 1 represents a weight loss ranging from 1% to 5%; 2 denotes a weight loss between 5% and 10%; 3 signifies a weight loss ranging from 10% to 15%; and 4 indicates a weight loss exceeding 15%.
The stool consistency score is categorized as follows: 0 represents firm stool; 1 indicates slightly soft stool; 2 denotes very soft but formed stool; 3 signifies very soft and unformed stool; and 4 represents watery diarrhea.
Bleeding score: 0 = none; 1 = mild occult blood in stools; 2 = moderate occult blood in stools; 3 = significant blood in stools; 4 = predominantly bloody stools.
In addition, mice were given 200 μL of 2.5% DSS by gavage twice daily, thus minimizing within-group variation due to differences in water intake. After 7 days, NCA029 was administered by gavage once daily for treatment. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.
IL-10 KO colitis model
Six-week-old germ-free male C57BL/6JGpt/-Il10em1Cd4885/Gp mice were used. After the twelfth week, mice were randomly divided into two experimental groups and monitored daily for the presence of spontaneous colitis. Specific parameters measured included body weight, fecal consistency, and presence/absence of fecal occult blood. Mice were treated with either a carrier (5% ethanol, 5% polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil 90% physiological saline) or 20 mg/kg of NCA029 once daily by oral gavage. At the end of the study, mice were euthanized, colon contents were extracted and removed, body weights and lengths were measured, and specimens were snap-frozen or formalin-fixed for subsequent analysis.

In the ITC experiments, a Nano-ITC system (manufactured by Nano, USA) was utilized. The experimental procedure entailed the gradual addition of the test compound into the sample cell at a concentration of 10 μM, with a volume of 200 μL. Following this, an injection syringe was employed to introduce 50 μL of HsClpP at a concentration of 100 μM into the sample cell, facilitating the titration process. The acquired data were subsequently subjected to fitting analysis utilizing LaunchNano Analyze software, leading to the determination of relevant parameters.

To investigate the binding affinity of NCA029 to HsClpP (PDB:
6DL7

a
−1

This was followed by a 500 ps NVT equilibrium and a 500 ps NPT equilibrium to confine the overall system positions. Finally, extensive MD simulations of 100 ns duration were performed at a temperature of 300 K.
Prior to simulation, energy minimization was executed using the Steepest Descent Method under vacuum conditions. The system was then immersed in a cubic water box, ensuring a 1.0 nm distance between the complex and the box’s edges. Charge neutralization of the system was achieved through the introduction of chloride or sodium ions. Protein structure and binding cavity analyses were conducted using PyMOL software.
